name: GE Power India Ltd
title: GE Power India Ltd - 532309 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Management pitches a demerger of the underutilised Durgapur boiler/coal-mill factory to JSW Energy (about 27 crore/yr loss, 2023-25) and a shift to services; no numeric FY27 guidance, and capacity exit is the only supply-side action.

utilisation.quote: the factory utilization has become limited largely to service work and non-coal activities

triggers.label: Durgapur capacity exited to JSW Energy
triggers.quote: the proposed demerger is the right path forward

triggers.label: Underutilised asset loss ~INR 27 cr/yr
triggers.quote: resulted in an average loss of approximately INR 27 crores per year

triggers.label: Demerger: 139 GEPIL shares → 10 JSW Energy
triggers.quote: For every 139 fully paid equity shares of GE Power India Limited, shareholders will receive 10 fully paid equity shares of JSW Energy

red_flags.label: Core manufacturing dependent on demerged entity
red_flags.quote: A five-year manufacturing services agreement with JSW Energy has been put in place to secure reserved capacity

red_flags.label: Supply chain independence not yet achieved
red_flags.quote: full supply chain independence targeted to be achieved soon

summary.headline: GE Power India proposes demerging its Durgapur business to JSW Energy, citing a ~INR 27 crore average annual loss from underutilisation, with 139:10 share entitlement.
summary.overview: Management presented a two-year turnaround narrative and the proposed demerger of the Durgapur business unit to JSW Energy under a scheme of arrangement. Net worth rose from INR 57 crore (Mar 2024) to INR 483 crore (Mar 2026), cash position reached INR 880 crore, and FY26 EBITDA was INR 277 crore versus a loss of INR 251 crore in FY23. Core services order booking grew to INR 734 crore in FY26 (about 34% YoY), and other OEM orders rose to about INR 322 crore. The demerger is effective retrospectively from 1 July 2025 on an as-is-where-is basis, subject to NCLT sanction. The call was a prepared presentation; no Q&A was held in the transcript provided.

segments.name: Core services
segments.commentary: Order bookings grew from INR 299 crore in FY22 to INR 734 crore in FY26, with management citing about 34% YoY growth in FY26 and a management priority on services-led, cash-accretive work.

segments.name: Other OEM services
segments.commentary: Order growth rose from about INR 162 crore to about INR 322 crore, with expansion into third-party fleets and international markets including Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Australia, UAE, Malaysia, Indonesia and Morocco.

segments.name: Durgapur business (to be demerged)
segments.commentary: Factory on about 661 acres of leasehold land in West Bengal, making boiler components, pressure vessels, piping and coal mills; utilisation limited mainly to service and non-coal work, with about INR 27 crore average annual loss from 2023 to 2025. Proposed transfer to JSW Energy.

guidance_outlook: Demerger effective retrospectively from 1 July 2025 on an as-is-where-is going-concern basis, subject to NCLT sanction.
Share entitlement: for every 139 GEPIL shares held, shareholders receive 10 JSW Energy shares; existing GEPIL holdings unchanged. Ratio backed by independent valuers and a fairness opinion.
Five-year manufacturing services agreement with JSW Energy for reserved capacity at pre-agreed schedule and pricing.
Full supply chain independence from Durgapur targeted 'soon', with efforts described as progressing very well; no date given.
Board unanimously approved the scheme; shareholders invited to vote. Timing of NCLT approval not stated.
capex_capacity: Durgapur site: about 661 acres leasehold, including industrial factory and residential township; factory utilisation low over 2023-2025.
Manufacturing and fabrication support for core services to come from JSW Energy-linked capacity under the five-year agreement while an independent supply chain is built.
No new capex or capacity-addition figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Core services order booking growth of about 34% YoY in FY26, with management stating it stopped chasing volume and prioritised value and profitability.
Other OEM segment order growth from about INR 162 crore to about INR 322 crore.
Management cited the broader demand outlook for the Indian power industry as supporting JSW Energy's use of the Durgapur facility.
No pricing or realisation data disclosed.
risks_watch: Shareholder and NCLT approval of the demerger scheme; timing not disclosed.
Continuity of manufacturing and fabrication for core services during the transition, given dependence on JSW Energy capacity until the independent supply chain is ready.
Execution of the five-year manufacturing services agreement on pre-agreed pricing.
Whether the INR 27 crore annual Durgapur loss stops from GEPIL's books post-demerger, and the resulting effect on reported profitability.
Sustainability of the 34% core services order growth and the INR 277 crore FY26 EBITDA base.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the turnaround and balance sheet repair, with a clear push for shareholder approval of the demerger. Management was reassuring on supply continuity but gave no timelines for NCLT approval or supply chain independence, so those remain soft.
key_quotes: Management does not expect any disruption to the manufacturing and fabrication support for the core services business.
For every 139 fully paid equity shares of GE Power India Limited, shareholders will receive 10 fully paid equity shares of JSW Energy.

growth.why: No numeric forward revenue guidance; management cites FY26 core services orders up about 34% YoY (INR 734 crore) and a five-year JSW Energy manufacturing agreement, but no new capacity or capex was disclosed and the Durgapur demerger removes an underutilised asset rather than adding capacity.
